correctness.rationale: For b≥3, two vertices in K_b×C_{2b+3} share a neighbor exactly when the cycle coordinates coincide or differ by ±2, so an injective coloring is a cycle of disjoint consecutive size-b fiber palettes after multiplication by 2. Since every color support is an independent set of size ≤b+1, bn=(2b+1)(b+1)−1 forces at least q=2b+1 colors. With exactly q, one deficient size-b support D and the other 2b supports size b+1 are forced by the unique missed-edge labels on the cycle; the converse construction gives every optimal coloring without multiplicity. A nontrivial one-vertex recolor occurs only where the same deficient color is absent from two adjacent edges, giving degree bΣ_j max(0,g_j−3). The gap lengths satisfy g_j=2+h_j, Σh_j=3, hence only excess compositions (3),(2,1),(1,1,1), degrees 2b,b,0. Ordered cycles of gaps give precisely the three stated counts multiplied by q!(b!)^n; the frozen fraction (b−1)(b−2)/((b+1)(b+2)) tends to 1. Independently enumerated all independent deficient sets and computed direct allowed recolorings for b=3 through 8; exact histograms match. All-b proof is combinatorial, not finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: New quantified statement is the exact three-degree reconfiguration distribution for every b≥3 at the optimal b-dependent palette, a refinement that neither the known injective chromatic number nor general frozen-H results imply. Converted the problem to b-fold proper colorings of an odd cycle, and compared the strongest general recoloring and Δ+1 frozen-fraction theorems with their actual hypotheses. No identified prior result supplies these counts; best-of-knowledge qualification and priority risks remain.

value.rationale: An exact freezing fraction approaching one at the minimum injective palette is a sharp, structurally motivated reconfiguration phenomenon, contrasting with different general-palette rarity settings. The one-defect support parametrization completely classifies local move degrees for a natural infinite product-graph family, providing exact data for coloring dynamics and combinatorial sampling. Neither a tiny calculation nor a mere chromatic-number substitution.
